channel.title: Quantum News | Quantum Research Center
channel.description: Quantum news and explainers for curious readers.

item.title: Intel agrees to buy quantum software company Classiq
item.description: Intel plans to pair Classiq’s algorithm-design software with its own silicon spin-qubit hardware. What the deal includes, what is still pending, and what it does not show.

item.title: Quantinuum reports a tenfold drop in logical error rate
item.description: A trapped-ion experiment runs a color code well below threshold, with about five errors per million operations on one logical qubit. What was shown, what it means for scaling, and what is still a goal.

item.title: US Department of War announces $350 million for quantum computing
item.description: New money for DARPA’s benchmarking programme, four more companies in its final evaluation stage, and a conditional loan to PsiQuantum. What each part is, and what it is not.

item.title: OpenAI claims a proof that Yang–Mills theory exists
item.description: A beginner’s guide to the Yang–Mills Millennium Problem, what OpenAI says its models proved and what it did not, why the mass gap remains open, and why the proof has not been released.

item.title: New York maps its quantum sector behind a $360 million commitment
item.description: A state-commissioned study ranks New York second in the US for quantum activity and estimates the economic return on its hubs. Which parts are funded, which are planned, and which are projections.

item.title: Exponential Time Hypothesis collapses
item.description: A beginner’s guide to the Exponential Time Hypothesis, how the algorithm OpenAI has released is claimed to work, which results it overturns and which survive, and why it is a statement about growth rates rather than a faster SAT solver.

item.title: Quantum-safe security starts with ordinary computers
item.description: Why preparing for quantum computers means changing the mathematics behind digital security.

item.title: India’s National Quantum Mission, explained
item.description: Computing is one part of a programme spanning communication, sensing, and the materials behind quantum devices.

item.title: Beyond the qubit count: how to read a quantum computing headline
item.description: A bigger processor is only part of the story. Reliability and the work a machine can actually perform matter too.
